technical-data.invention-title: DISPENSING DEVICE FOR A CONTAINER AND METHOD OF MANUFACTURING AND FILLING SUCH A CONTAINER WITH DOSING AND/OR FILLING HEAD
DISTRIBUTEUR DESTINE A UN RECIPIENT ET PROCEDE DE FABRICATION ET DE REMPLISSAGE DE CE RECIPIENT AU MOYEN D'UNE TETE DE DOSAGE ET/OU DE REMPLISSAGE

abstract.p: The invention relates to a dispensing device to be connected to a container for dosed dispensing of a fluid, comprising an opening and a closing member coacting with the opening and movable between a position closing the opening and a position leaving clear the opening, part of the dispensing device being integrally preformed on a neck of the container, and the remaining part of the dispensing device being connected thereto. The part of the dispensing device preformed on the neck part may comprise means for fixedly holding the closing member in one of its positions and/or means for biasing the closing member to one of its positions. The dispensing device may further comprise a pump arranged between the container and the opening and movable means connected to the pump for operating thereof, with part of the operating means being preformed on the container. The dispensing device may also include a precompression system arranged between the pump and the discharge nozzle, the pump, the precompression system and part of the conduits connecting the pump to the container and/or the discharge nozzle being integrally formed. The invention further relates to a method of manufacturing and filling with a fluid a container with such a dispensing device, comprising the steps of: forming the container, preforming a part of the dispensing device on a neck part thereof, forming the remaining part of the dispensing device, filling the container with the fluid, and closing the container by connecting the remaining part of the dispensing device thereto. The container may be preformed by means of injection molding and may be blow molded into its final form prior to filling thereof.

L'invention concerne un distributeur destiné à être relié à un récipient et servant à la distribution dosée d'un fluide. Ce distributeur comprend un orifice et un organe d'obturation qui coopère avec l'orifice et se déplace entre une position d'obturation de l'orifice et une position d'ouverture de l'orifice. Une partie du distributeur est préformée intégralement avec un goulet du récipient, la partie restante étant reliée audit goulet. La partie du distributeur préformée avec le goulet peut comprendre un système pour fixer l'organe d'obturation dans l'une des positions et/ou un système pour solliciter l'organe d'obturation en direction de l'une de ces positions. En outre, le distributeur peut comprendre une pompe aménagée entre le récipient et l'orifice et déplaçable entre le système relié à la pompe et servant à l'actionner, une partie du système d'actionnement étant préformée sur le récipient. Le dispositif de distribution peut aussi comprendre un système de précompression disposé entre la pompe et la buse de décharge, la pompe, le système de précompression et une partie des conduits reliant la pompe au récipient et/ou à la buse de décharge étant intégralement formés. L'invention concerne aussi un procédé pour fabriquer et remplir avec un fluide un récipient pourvu de ce distributeur qui consiste à faire ce qui suit: former le récipient; préformer une partie du distributeur sur sa partie goulet; former la partie restante du distributeur; remplir le récipient avec un fluide et; fermer le récipient en y reliant la partie restante du distributeur. Le récipient peut être préformé au moyen de moulage par injection et moulé par soufflage dans sa forme finale avant le remplissage.

description.p: DISPENSING DEVICE FOR A CONTAINER AND METHOD OF MANUFACTURING AND FILLING SUCH A CONTAINER WITH DOSING
AND/OR FILLING HEAD

The invention relates to a dispensing device to be connected to a container for dosed dispensing of a fluid, comprising at least one opening and at least one closing member co-acting with the opening and movable between a position closing the opening and a position leaving clear the opening. Such a dispensing device is known, for instance in the form of a head for a water bottle or drinking bottle.
The term "fluid" is understood in this text to mean any non-gaseous flowing medium, therefore liquids as well as finely distributed, powdery solid materials.

The known dispensing device is generally releasably connected to the container, for instance screwed onto the neck of the container, after the container has been formed and filled. The dispensing device, which forms an independent unit, is generally formed separately or assembled from a number of components .

The known dispensing device thus has the drawback that it has a relatively large number of components and both the forming and assembly thereof with the (filled) container is relatively difficult. Both the manufacture and the assembly of the dispensing device are hereby expensive and time-consuming, which represents a particular drawback now that increasingly larger numbers of such drinking bottles are being used.

The invention therefore has for its object to provide a dispensing device for a container of the above described type, wherein the above stated drawbacks do not occur. According to the invention this is achieved in that at least a part of the dispensing device is preformed on a neck part of the container, and the
remaining part of the dispensing device is connected thereto. Already fixing a part of the dispensing device beforehand to a neck part of the container achieves that the assembly of the dispensing device in fact coincides with mounting of the dispensing device on the container, whereby in all fewer operations are required. In addition, the remaining part of the dispensing device can take a lighter and simpler form than in conventional dispensing devices, since it will not be used or handled as an independent part and can thus derive its strength and rigidity from the container.

The part of the dispensing device preformed on the neck part of the container is preferably formed integrally with this neck part. In this manner the number of separate components is reduced and assembly thus simplified. A further reduction in the number of components is obtained when the neck part in turn is formed integrally with the container.

The part of the dispensing device preformed on the neck part can for instance comprise means for fixedly holding the closing member in at least one of its positions, or means for biasing the closing member to one of its positions. Such biasing means can advantageously comprise at least one spring. In another embodiment, the dispensing device further includes at least one pump arranged between the container and the opening, said pump having a suction side and a compression side, said dispensing device further comprising movable means connected to the pump for operating thereof, means connected to the suction side of the pump for supplying fluid from the container and at least one discharge nozzle connected to the compression side of the pump. The dispensing device thus forms a sprayer head as known from spray bottles, for instance for detergents.

The prior art sprayer head comprises a body that may be fixed, usually screwed onto the neck of a container or bottle and in which a manually operable
piston pump is arranged. For operating the pump a trigger is hingedly connected to the body. The suction side of the pump is connected to a tube that extends into the bottle over a substantial length, usually to a position near the bottom, and through which a fluid, typically a liquid may be drawn out of the bottle. The compression side of the pump is connected to a discharge nozzle of the sprayer head through a conduit. A return element, typically a biasing spring is arranged in the pump so as to force the piston back to its position of rest at the end of a pump stroke. The prior art sprayer head is usually screwed onto the bottle in the filling line, after the bottle has been completely filled.

This conventional sprayer head has the drawback of having a relatively high number of parts and being relatively hard to assemble. Thus both manufacture and assembly of the sprayer head are costly and time- consuming, which is especially inconvenient in view of the increasing number of spray bottles being used. Furthermore, the various parts of the prior art sprayer head are made of different materials, which poses a problem in handling and recycling the spray bottle after it has been discarded.

The above-mentioned drawbacks are now obviated in the dispensing device or sprayer head in accordance with the present invention by the fact that at least part of the sprayer head is preformed with the container and the remaining part of the sprayer head is attached thereto. The part of the dispensing device preformed with the container may advantageously comprise at least part of the operating means. When for instance the pump is a piston pump and the piston of the pump is connected with means for biasing it to a position of rest, these piston biasing means, which may advantageously comprise at least one spring, are preferably attached to the container. A structurally simple embodiment is then
obtained when the spring is a flexion and/or torsion spring.

In order to simplify assembling of the dispensing device and improve its functioning the piston biasing means are advantageously adapted for cooperation with the operating means of the pump. In that manner the piston biasing means need not extend into or be arranged in the pump. Thus the air filled space within the pump occupied by conventional piston biasing springs is suppressed, whereby the pumping action is improved. Furthermore, the choice of materials for the piston biasing means is less critical, as these will not be in contact with the fluid.

It is noted that in this case the operating means are preferably connected to the piston such as to be fixed under tension and compression, for instance snapped onto the piston, in order to have it follow all movements of the operating means.

The pump advantageously has a housing to which the operating means are movably connected. An easy to assemble dispensing device is then obtained when the operating means comprise a trigger hingedly snapped onto the pump housing.

In a variant of this embodiment, the pump comprises a work cylinder and a vent cylinder arranged next thereto and the operating means are arranged for displacing the pistons in these cylinders in synchronized fashion. In that case the operating means preferably comprise a pusher member and the or each piston is integrally formed with the pusher member.

In accordance with another aspect of the invention the metering device comprises blocking means cooperating with the operating means, which blocking means may comprise at least one frangible tongue arranged in a path of the operating means or a cover closing off the discharge nozzle.

In accordance with yet another aspect of the invention the dispensing device is provided with a
precompression system arranged between the pump and the discharge nozzle, and the pump, the precompression system and part of the conduits connecting the pump to the container and/or the discharge nozzle are integrally formed.

A very simple assembly is achieved when the remaining part of the dispensing device is connected by means of a snap coupling to the neck part of the container or to the part of the dispensing device preformed thereon. In this manner the connection between both these parts can be brought about quickly and simply in a single movement.

In yet another embodiment of the invention a feed member which is in fluid connection with the container and has at least one outlet opening, and a dosing member connected fluid-tight to the feed member and having at least one outlet opening debouching in a dosing chamber, wherein the feed member and the dosing member are rotatable relative to each other in order to determine different doses.
This embodiment of the invention constitutes a dispensing cap for a squeeze-bottle which is filled with fluid.

By rotating the feed member and dosing member, the outlet opening of the dosing member can be placed in register with the outlet opening of the feed member. If the bottle is then squeezed, the fluid will be pushed upward into the feed member and will subsequently flow through the outlet openings of the feed member and the dosing member into the dosing chamber. When the pressure on the squeeze-bottle is removed, the fluid will, owing to the underpressure in the interior of the bottle, be sucked back out of the dosing chamber through the outlet openings of the dosing and feed members. This return suction of the fluid is ended the moment air is drawn in. This will be the case when the relevant outlet opening of the dosing member comes above the fluid level in the dosing chamber. The choice of the height of the outlet
openings which are placed in register thus determines the liquid level which will remain in the dosing chamber after release of the squeeze-bottle and which can then be poured out and used. This dosing device, which enables dosing of liquids in simple manner and with relatively great accuracy, can for instance be used to administer food or medication to animals and to measure off required quantities of cleaning agents and the like. In a preferred embodiment of this dispensing device the feed member and the dosing member each comprise a substantially cylindrical sidewall, whereby sealing between the members is improved. Preferably, the feed member has an axial channel recessed into its cylindrical side wall and the dosing member includes a plurality of outlet openings spaced in both peripheral and axial direction, so that different doses of fluid may be dispensed.
Further preferred embodiments of the dosing device according to this embodiment of the invention are described in the dependent claims 30-37.

The dosing chamber and the container are preferably preformed by means of injection molding and the container is herein advantageously blow molded to an end form after the preforming. A preformed container with a part of the dosing device already thereon is thus obtained, which can be stored and transported easily and can moreover be assembled with a small number of operations to form a complete end product. The invention further relates to an assembly of a (neck part of a) container and a dispensing device as described above connected thereto. Such an assembly is simple and can be manufactured at low cost, has fewer components than usual and can in addition be relatively light.

The invention also relates to a container for use in an assembly as described above. Such a container, on which a part of the dispensing device is thus
preformed, provides the above discussed advantages in respect of ease of assembly, cost price and the like when compared to conventional containers, which are provided only with provisions for fixing a dispensing device, for instance in the form of screw thread round their neck. Finally, the invention relates to a method of manufacturing and filling with a fluid a container with a dispensing device. Such a method is also generally known. In the conventional method the container or bottle is formed at a first location, generally by means of blow molding, and supplied to a filling line. The bottle is herein usually provided with fixing means such as screw thread in the vicinity of the filling opening or neck thereof. The dispensing device, which is constructed from a relatively large number of different components, is assembled at another location and herein also provided with fixing means such as screw thread. This head is then supplied in fully assembled form to the filling line. On the filling line the bottle is filled, whereafter the head is fixed, thus for instance screwed, thereon.

This known method has the drawback that the manufacturing and filling of the container and dispensing device require a relatively large number of operations, which are not geared to each other and cannot be integrated either, whereby the method is therefore time- consuming and expensive. In addition, complete assemblies are already formed at a relatively early stage in the known method which have a relatively high value compared to the end product, which results in the cost of possible rejects at a later stage being relatively high. Finally, once they have been manufactured the empty containers take up a relatively large amount of space during transport and storage before they are filled.

The invention therefore has for its object to provide a method of the described type, wherein said drawbacks do not occur. This is achieved according to the invention with a method which comprises the steps of forming the container, preforming a part of the
dispensing device on a neck part thereof, forming the remaining part of the dispensing device, filling the container and closing thereof by connecting the remaining part of the dispensing device thereto. By performing in this manner a part of the assembly of the dispensing device only on the filling line, the total number of operations is reduced, which results in an increase in productivity and a decrease in costs.

The part of the dispensing device preformed on the neck part is preferably formed integrally and simultaneously therewith. The number of components is thus reduced and assembly thus simplified and accelerated. This is even more the case when the neck part is also formed integrally and simultaneously with the container.

When the container is preformed by means of injection molding and is inflated to its final form before filling thereof, the space occupied by the containers prior to filling is reduced, which results in a decrease in the cost of transport and storage.

Furthermore, parts of the dispensing device of relatively complicated form can be formed simultaneously and integrally with the container in simple manner by injection molding. The container is then advantageously manufactured herein from a resiliently deformable thermoplastic material, for instance PET, so that the components of the dosing head integrated therewith can be embodied robustly while the container can be inflated simply. A method which is quick and easy to perform is obtained when the remaining part of the dispensing device is connected by means of a snap coupling to the neck part of the container or the part of the dispensing device preformed thereon, since both parts can then be mutually connected in a single movement.

The container is preferably filled in suspended position. In contrast to the conventional method of filling, wherein the containers are transported and
filled in standing position, a machine used for filling does not hereby have to be adapted when containers with a different volume and thus a different height have to be processed. In a further preferred embodiment, the remaining part of the dispensing device includes a pump having a displacement element that is moveable between first and second positions, the displaceable element being moved to its second position before the container is closed and being moved to its first position after the container is closed, such as to draw fluid into the pump. The dispenser, formed by the container with its dispensing device is then ready for use.

A container 1 with part 2 of a dispensing device 3 preformed thereon is formed according to the invention by first injection molding these in the form of a "test tube", the so-called "preform" 4 (figure 1), and by then inflating this preform 4 to the actual container. As stated, preform 4 already comprises a part of the dispensing device 3, in the embodiment shown a cup-shaped receiving part 2 in which the remaining part 5 of dispensing device 3 is received slidably. This cup-shaped part 2 is further provided with means for fixedly holding
slidable part 5 in two end positions, in the form of two grooves 6, 7 which co-act with a rib 8 arranged on slidable part 5.

In the embodiment shown the remaining part 5 of dispensing device 3 forms the closure for an outlet opening 9 of container 1. It comprises a cylindrical body with a continuous outlet channel 10, a thickened handling edge 11 and the actual closing member 12, which is suspended by means of ribs 13 in the middle of outlet channel 10 while leaving clear passage openings on all sides and which has a chamfered end edge 14 which fits closely into the neck 15 of container 1.

When the content of container 1 must thus be poured, the part 5 is moved outward from the position shown in figure 3, in which outlet opening 9 is closed by closing member 12 and in which part 5 is held fixedly by co-action of rib 8 with the one groove 7, by pulling on handling edge 11 until rib 8 falls into the other groove 6 (figure 2) . In this position closing member 12 is situated at a distance from the edge 15 of the neck, and outlet opening 9 is thus left clear. The content of container 1 can then flow round closing member 12 through outlet channel 10.

In another embodiment of assembly 17 of container 1 and dispensing device 3 according to the invention, two handling parts or handles 16 are also formed on the (preform of the) container simultaneously with forming of preform 4 and part 2 of head 3 formed integrally therewith (figures 4, 5). This is particularly important for relatively large containers with a content of several liters, such as for instance packagings for soft drinks, beer or wine. These handles 16 can take different forms, such as can be seen in figures 8 and 9. More or fewer than two handles 16 can of course also be co-formed with the container.

As stated above, container 1 with the part 2 of head 3 preformed thereon is formed in the embodiment shown in that a relatively thick-walled preform 4 of the
container and an integral part of dispensing device 3 is formed first at a first location 18 by any suitable manufacturing technique, for instance by injection molding, optionally in combination with other co-molded components such as handles (figure 12, block 19). Because this preform 4 has a considerably smaller volume than the container 1 to be finally formed, the costs of transport and/or storage thereof are relatively low. This way of forming the container has the added advantage of allowing parts to be connected to the container by sliding them onto the preform 4, so that they will be fixedly clamped between the dispensing device 3 and the container 1 after the latter has been inflated to its final shape.

The remaining part 5 of dispensing device 3 is further formed at the same or another location 20 by means of any suitable technique, for instance injection molding (block 21) . After cooling and removal from the injection mould, the different parts are then transported (block 22) to another location 23, where filling and final assembly take place.

The part 5 of head 3 is fed via a buffer 24 to a positioning station 25. The preform 4 having integrated therewith the part 2 of head 3 and possible other components is fed from block 26 to a filling line, where at a first station 27 the preform 4 is heated and then inflated to form a container 1 with the desired final shape. For this purpose preform 4 has a handling edge, in the shown embodiment the protruding underside 37 of cup- shaped part 2, on which it can be picked up and clamped. This is therefore a two-stage process for blow molding of container 1. It is however also possible to form the container in a one-stage process, wherein in one and the same machine preform 4 is injection molded and, while still warm, inflated to its final form. After progressing through a buffer 28 the thus formed container 1 is then filled in a subsequent station 29 with a fluid, generally a liquid, for instance a soft drink, a liquid cleaning product or the like. The
presence of edge 37 is an advantage herein, since container 1 can be suspended therefrom in the filling machine. In contrast to conventional filling stations, in which container 1 is transported in standing position, this filling station 29 does not therefore have to be adapted when containers of a different volume, and thus a different height, have to be processed.

Finally, in a following station 30 the filled container 1 is closed by arranging thereon the remaining part 5 of dispensing device 3. The thus formed assembly 17 then progresses further through the usual steps of labelling (block 31) , packing into boxes (block 32) and palletizing and shrink-wrapping (block 33) , wherein the usual buffers 34, 35 and 36 are present between these steps.

In another embodiment the dispensing device is a sprayer head 101 for a container 102 (figure 14) comprising a pump 103 having a suction side 105 and a compression side 106. Movable operating means 104 are connected to the pump 103, in the illustrated example constituted by a trigger 113 having a hook part 115 snapped around a pivot shaft 114. Means 107 are connected to the suction side 105 of the pump 103 for supplying a fluid from the container, comprised of a conduit having its free end connected to a tube 123 extending into the container. The compression side 106 of the pump 103 is connected to a discharge nozzle 108 through a conduit 109. In the illustrated embodiment pump 103, operating means 104 and discharge nozzle 108 are arranged in a frame 122, which can be fixed to the container 102 in a way to be discussed below.

Pump 103 is a piston pump, constituted by a pump housing or cylinder 110 and a piston 111 reciprocating therein. The piston 111 is connected to a piston rod 112 which in turn is connected to the trigger 113. In order to return the piston 111 and trigger 113 to their extended position of rest at the end of a pump stroke, the sprayer head 101 comprises biasing means 116.
In the illustrated embodiment the biasing means are constituted by a plurality of parallel flexion springs 117 that engage the trigger 113. When the trigger 113 is pivoted around the pivot shaft 114 towards the pump 103 and presses the piston 111 into the cylinder 110 during a pump stroke, the springs 117 are bent. When the pressure on the trigger 113 is released it is forced back to its position of rest by the springs 117 flexing back. Since the trigger is connected to the piston 111 such as to remain fixed under both tension and compression, the piston 111 is then also pulled back to its position of rest. The connection between the trigger 113 and the piston 111 is formed by the piston rod 112, which is snapped onto the piston 111 and is connected to the trigger 113 by means of a film hinge. The snap connection between the piston rod 112 and the piston 111 is formed by a head 127 of the piston rod 112 being snapped into a corresponding opening 128 in the piston 111.

The springs 117 each have a closed contour and are fixed on one end 118 to a column or "spine" 119 whereas the opposite side of each spring 117 has a protrusion 124 engaging in a cavity 125 in the trigger 113. The column 119 which consists of a curved web 120 and a reinforcing rib arranged therein, has a partly cylindrical basis 129 which is attached to the neck 130 of the container 102. The basis 129, the column 119 and the springs 117 are integrally molded with the container 102. In the basis 129 two opposite openings 131 are arranged which cooperate with two protruding snap members 32 on the frame 122 carrying the pump 103, the operating means 104 and the discharge nozzle 108. This frame 122 further comprises a cylindrical lower part or skirt 133 which may be close fittingly received in the neck 130 of the container 102 an there constitutes a gas- and liquid tight seal with the inner edge 134 of that neck. The frame 122 further comprises an edge 135 and a shoulder 143 which in the assembled state of the sprayer head 101 come to rest on the upper edge 136 of the neck 130.
Since part of the sprayer head 101, in the shown embodiment the biassing means 116 form part of the container 102, assembling the sprayer head 101 finally takes place on the moment that the container 102 is filled and subsequently closed by placing the frame 122 carrying the various parts of the sprayer head 101. Since part of the operations relating to assembly of the sprayer head 101 are in fact integrated with the final assembly which are also necessary, the total number of operations to be performed for forming the container with the sprayer head is substantially lower than with conventional, completely pre-assembled sprayer heads. Furthermore, the number of sperate parts is substantially reduced in comparison to a conventional sprayer head, since certain parts are integrated in the container. For assembling the remaining parts of the sprayer head the flexion springs 117 must be introduced into the cavity 125 of the trigger 113. To this end the piston 111 must be moved to its outer position. Then the remaining part of the sprayer head 101 may be pressed into the neck of the container 102 and fixed therein by means of the snap members 132 engaging in the openings 131.

In another embodiment of the assembly of sprayer head 101 and container 102, which is the preferred embodiment at the moment (Figure 18) , the biassing means 116 take the shape of separate flexion springs 117 extending substantially parallel to the longitudinal of axis of the container 102, instead of perpendicular thereto as in the first embodiment. These flexion springs 117 cooperate with ribs 152 arranged in the cavity 125 of the trigger 113. In this embodiment the trigger 113 has a continuous pivot shaft 153 that is received in a hollow space 154 in the frame 122 and that is locked therein by a flexible snap arm 155. As the shaft 153 of the trigger 113 and the receiving space 154 are located above the spraying conduit 109, an aperture 156 is arranged in the trigger 113 , through which extends
the end of this conduit 109, onto which is arranged the discharge nozzle 108. The trigger further comprises protruding cams 157 which directly engage in openings 68 of the piston 111. This embodiment therefore has no separate piston rod.

On the other hand it is also possible, for instance when the container 102 and the springs 117 are made of a material that is less flexible, to use combined flexion and torsion springs that are deformable in various directions instead of the flexion springs 117 as shown (Figure 22) . Such combined flexion and torsion springs 117 comprise in the shown embodiment a bracket
169 connected to the container 102 and a torsion spring

170 arranged perpendicular thereto, which extends in two directions. The actual flexion springs 117 are attached to the free ends 171 of the torsion spring 170 and have a curved shape in themselves, for instance an inverted U- shape. In this way the springs 117 may also be molded integrally with the container 102 when this is made of a less flexible material.

Furthermore, in this embodiment a precompression system is shown to be arranged between the cylinder 110 and the spraying conduit 109 comprising an annular space 158 connected to the cylinder 110 and closed off in a gas- and liquid-tight manner by a resiliently flexible diaphragm 159. The space 158 is bordered by a cylindrical sleeve 160 that is received in a cavity 161 in the frame 122 and that is integrally formed with the diaphragm 159 in the illustrated embodiment. In this cylindrical sleeve 160 an opening 162 is formed, in which is arranged a movable valve 163, and which is connected to the suction conduit 107 for the fluid through an opening 167 in the frame 122. In the shown embodiment this valve 163, which may hermetically seal the opening 167, is also integrally formed with the sleeve 160. Further a stop member 164 is connected to the diaphragm 159, which serves to limit bending of the diaphragm 159. The cylindrical sleeve 160 is locked in
the cavity 161 of the frame 122 by an end wall which is integrally molded with the container 102.

The precompression system 140 serves in known manner to inhibit transport of fluid from the container 102 to the discharge nozzle as long as a predetermined pump pressure is not yet attained. If a fluid is sprayed through the nozzle 108 at too low a pressure, this fluid is insufficiently atomized and drops generated in the spray cone are too large. In order to prevent this from occurring the connection between the container 102 and the discharge nozzle 108 is closed off by the diaphragm 159 which is forcibly pressed against the rim 166 of the spraying conduit 109 serving as a seat due to the internal stress determined by the domed configuration and assisted by the ambient pressure behind the diaphragm 159. Only when sufficient pressure, for instance on the order of 3 bar, is built up in the cylinder 110 by moving the piston 111 to its end position will the diaphragm 159 be lifted from the seat 166. The sprayer head 101 thus functions as follows.

When a user wishes to atomize the fluid from the container 102, he first pulls the trigger 113. In this way air that is present in the cylinder 110 and that cannot flow back to the container 102 due to the opening 167 being shut off by the valve 163 is compressed by the piston 111. When the pressure of the air is high enough at the end of the pump stroke the diaphragm 159 is lifted from the seat 166 and the air may escape.

During the subsequent return stroke forced by the biasing means 116 fluid is drawn from the container 102 through tube 123, conduit 107 and openings 162 and 167 into the cylinder 110 until this is completely filled at the end of the return or suction stroke (Figure 18A) . In order to prevent a partial vacuum from being developed in the container 102 during this stroke an aeration hole 151 is formed in the wall of the cylinder 110, which is opened when an outer peripheral sealing lip 139B passes the opening 151 during inward movement of the piston 111
and which is again connected to a closed space defined between the outer and inner peripheral sealing lips 139B and 139A of the piston 111 during the outward stroke of the piston 111. The sprayer head 101 in accordance with this embodiment of the invention is assembled by inserting the annular sleeve 160 and the suction tube 123 into the injection molded frame 122. Then the piston 111 is slid into the cylinder 110 and the trigger 113 is snapped with its pivot shaft 153 into the hollow 154 of the frame 122. After that the trigger 113 and the piston 111 are snapped together, after which finally the discharge nozzle 108 may be attached to the end of the spraying conduit 109. The assembly thus formed may then simply be introduced into the neck of the container 102 until the snap member 132 of the frame 122 snap into the openings 131 in the cheeks 129 above the neck 130 of the container 102. This embodiment is thus easier to assemble than the first embodiment. The total path of forming, assembling and filling the container 102 and the sprayer head 101 is thus as follows. At a first location 144 the frame 122 carrying the cylinder 110 of the pump 103, the suction conduit 107 and the spraying conduit 109 is injection molded (figure 25, block 174) . Also the trigger 113

(block 175) , piston 111 (block 176) , sleeve 160 (block 177) and discharge nozzle 108 (block 178) are formed by any suitable technique, for instance injection molding. All these parts are assembled in block 179. If so desired also the suction tube 123 may already be mounted (block 180) .

At the same location or a different location the container 102 is preformed (block 181) , as well as the part of the sprayer head integrated therewith, in the embodiment illustrated above the biasing means 116. The various parts are then transported (block 182) to a different location, where the filling and final assembly operations are performed.
The part of the sprayer head that has already been assembled (block 183) is provided with a suction tube 123 supplied from a block 184 at a station 185, unless of course this had already been done previously. Then the thus formed subassembly is supplied to a positioning station 190 via a buffer 187. The test-tube like preform 146 with integrated biasing means 116 is supplied to a filling line from a block 186. All further steps correspond to those described in relation to the first embodiment and shown in Figure 12. However, it is also possible to "prime" the dispenser, by filling the pump with some liquid drawn from the container. To this end the piston of the pump is pushed inward before assembly of the dispensing device and the container, and is then pulled outward during or after assembly, thus drawing liquid from the container into the pump. The dispenser is then ready for use.

In yet another embodiment of the invention, which may also be used for conventional bottles having a threaded neck, some parts of the sprayer head are pre- assembled or integrated not with the neck of the container, but rather with a separate ring 172 (figure 23) . This ring 172 may then be fixed to the neck of a conventional bottle 173 (figure 24) . While it is true that the advantage of a simplified assembly is lost to some extent in this case, the advantages with respect to the limited number of parts in the sprayer head remain.

The device 202 for metered dispensing of a liquid or gel from a container 201 in accordance with yet another embodiment of the invention comprises a pump 203, a suction side 204 of which is connected to the container 201 through a suction conduit 205, whereas the pressure side 206 thereof is connected to a stationary discharge nozzle 208 through a pressure conduit 207. In the illustrated embodiment the dispensing device 202 is meant for a gel like hand soap and the discharge nozzle 208 takes the form of an outflow tube.
The pump 203 comprises two cylinders arranged next to each other, a work cylinder 209 and a vent cylinder 210. In each of the cylinders 209, 210 a piston 211, 212 is displaceably arranged. The vent cylinder 210 includes a ridge 236 for deforming the piston 212 at the end of its stroke, thus creating a venting gap. Both pistons are operated by operating means 213, in this case in the shape of an upwardly and downwardly moveable pusher member. In this embodiment both pistons are rigidly connected to, and even integrally formed with the operating member 213.

The operating member 213 is moveable in upward and downward direction between a position of rest and a pumping position. From this pumping position the pusher member is returned to its position of rest when the pressure is released therefrom by return means 214, which in this embodiment are also formed by two combined flexion and torsion springs 215 that are integrally formed with the container 201. Between the pump 203 and the discharge nozzle

208 a precompression system 216 is also arranged. This precompression system again comprises a diaphragm 217 which forms part of a sleeve 218 arranged in a chamber 220, in which is also arranged a moveable shut-off valve 219. The sleeve 218 is fixed in the chamber 220 by a retainer 237 forming part of a cup-shaped part 230 that is integrally formed with the container 201.

The pump 203, the chamber 220 of the precompression system and part of the suction and pressure lines 205, 207 are formed as a single injection molded piece 231, that is received in the cup-shaped part 230. To this end the piece 223 has two mounting wings 232 which are received in slots 233 arranged in the cup- shaped part 230. In this way, the number of separate parts is reduced and the assembly is simplified. Also problems in respect of possible leakage are hereby minimized.
The dispensing device 202 further comprises blocking means 221 by which unauthorized use of device 202 may be prevented or at least rendered detectable after the act. In a first embodiment of the device 202 these blocking means are constituted by two frangible tongues 222 that are arranged in the path of the operating member 213 and that are integrally formed with the outflow tube 8. The tongues are arranged on an gripping part 23 that may be manipulated by a user so as to bring it out of the path of the operating member and tearing it off, whereby the pusher member 13 may be pressed down and the pump 3 may be operated. As the tongues 22 have to be torn off before use, any (possibly unauthorized) use will always be immediately detectable. It is also possible to integrate the blocking means 21 or frangible tongues 22 with the operating member 13 (fig. 30) . In that case the discharge nozzle 208 may be integrally formed with the pressure conduit 207 and the number of parts may be further reduced. In yet another embodiment (fig. 35) the blocking means 221 are formed by a cover 224 that is hingedly connected to the pusher member 213 (fig. 37) and that closes off the discharge nozzle and comes to lie in a correspondingly shaped recess 225, so that the pusher member 213 is latched against further movement. This embodiment may very well be combined with a discharge nozzle 228 that is embodied as a spraying or atomizing element (fig. 36) and that is formed by a cylindrical sleeve 226 having a very small metering orifice 227. In yet another embodiment (Figure 44) , the return means 214 comprise four flexion springs 215 having inwardly inclined engagement surfaces 234. The pusher member 213 of this embodiment has corresponding inclined surfaces 235 cooperating with the springs 215. When the pusher member 213 is pushed down during an inward compression stroke the springs 215 are bent inward by the inclined surfaces 235 travelling downwards. When the pusher member 213 is released the springs 215 flex back,
causing the pusher member 213 and thus the piston 211 to travel upwards again. The other parts of this embodiment correspond with those of the previous embodiment, and are not described here in further detail. A device 302 for dosed dispensing of a quantity of fluid from a container 301 in accordance with another alternative embodiment of the invention (fig. 38) comprises a dosing chamber 303, at least the side wall 306 of which is formed integrally with container 301. Arranged in dosing chamber 303 is a dosing member 304 which is in communication with the interior of the container by means of an immersion tube 316 which is placed in the underside 323 of dosing member 304 and extends to a position close to the bottom 318 of container 301. Dosing member 304 is fixed to or formed integrally with a disc-like part 307 which functions as bottom of dosing chamber 303. This disc-like part 307 is provided with a skirt 308 which is arranged along the periphery and with which it can be received sealingly in a narrowed neck 321 between container 301 and dosing chamber 303. The disc-like part 307 is further provided with a longitudinal groove 326 which is intended to be positioned around a longitudinal rib 328 extending into the dosing chamber 303, such as to fix the disc-like part against rotation in dosing chamber 303. A second member 305 is rotatably received in dosing member 304. This second member 305 is fixed to or formed integrally with a cover 311 which closes dosing chamber 303 at the top and is rotatable relative to dosing chamber 303. Cover 311 can be fixed for instance by means of a snap connection 324, 325 to the wall 6 of dosing chamber 303.

In the cylindrical body 309 of dosing member 304 a number of outlet openings 310 are arranged distributed in peripheral direction and at different heights. The likewise cylindrical second member 305 is provided with a channel 320 which is recessed into its cylinder wall 322 and which can be placed in register with one of the outlet openings 310 of dosing member 304
by rotating this member 305 relative to dosing member 304. In the position shown in figures 39 and 40, channel 320 of second member 305 is not in register with one of the outlet openings 310 of dosing member 4 so that there is therefore no liquid connection between the interior of container 301 and dosing chamber 303. Cover 311 is moreover formed in the shown embodiment such that in this position a triangular protruding part 313 of cover 311 co-acts sealingly with an outlet opening or spout 312 of dosing chamber 303. Leakage is thus wholly prevented. Further arranged in cover 311 is a venting aperture 314 which in the opened position of dosing device 302 ensures that air can penetrate into dosing chamber 303 when it is emptied but which in the shown closed position is also closed by a cam 315 arranged on the upper edge of a rib 328 protruding into dosing chamber 303.

The operation of dosing device 302 is therefore as follows. When, starting from the closed position shown in figures 39 and 40, the cover 311 with the second member 305 is rotated, and dosing member 304 is held against rotation by its grove 326 and the rib 328, channel 320 of this second member 305 can be placed in register with one of the outlet openings 310 of dosing member 304, whereby a liquid connection is formed between container 301 and dosing chamber 303. The reaching of such a position is indicated by markings 317 which are arranged on outer wall 306 of dosing chamber 303 and which in the relevant position lie precisely in register with the triangular closing part 313 of cover 311. If container 301 is squeezed in this position, liquid is then carried through immersion tube 316 via an opening 319 in the bottom of dosing chamber 303 to dosing member 304 and then flows via channel 320 and the relevant outlet opening 310 into dosing chamber 303. Container 301 must herein be squeezed for so long that the liquid level in dosing chamber 303 lies in any case above the relevant outlet opening 310. If container 301 is then released liquid will then be sucked back, as a result of the
underpressure prevailing therein, from dosing chamber 303 via outlet opening 310 and channel 320 to immersion tube 316, and finally to container 301. This return suction takes place for as long as outlet opening 310 lies below the liquid surface. When the liquid level in dosing chamber 303 reaches the top of outlet opening 310, air will then be drawn in, whereafter the liquid flow from dosing chamber 303 to container 301 stops. At that moment a precisely determined quantity of liquid remains behind in dosing chamber 303 which can subsequently be poured out through spout 312.

As stated, container 301 and dosing chamber 303 are formed integrally. After the container 301 has been formed and filled with liquid the other components can be pressed or snapped fixedly into container 301 and dosing chamber 303, whereafter container 301 with dosing device 302 is ready for use.

Although the invention has been described above with reference to a number of possible embodiments thereof, the skilled person will appreciate that many modifications could be made thereto. In particular, the novel and inventive features of the dispensers that are not directly related to the integration of part of the dispensing device with the container could be applied with equal effect to conventional, separately produced dispensers. The scope of the invention is therefore defined solely by the appended claims.

claim.claim-text: CLAIMS

1. Dispensing device to be connected to a container for dosed dispensing of a fluid, comprising at least one opening and at least one closing member co- acting with the opening and movable between a position closing the opening and a position leaving clear the opening, characterized in that at least a part of the dispensing device is preformed on a neck part of the container, and the remaining part of the dispensing device is connected thereto. 2. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 1, characterized in that the part of the dispensing device preformed on the neck part is formed integrally with the neck part.
3. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 1 or 2 , characterized in that the neck part is formed integrally with the container.

4. Dispensing device as claimed in any of the foregoing claims, characterized in that the part of the dispensing device preformed on the neck part comprises means for fixedly holding the closing member in at least one of its positions.

5. Dispensing device as claimed in any of the foregoing claims, characterized in that the part of the dispensing device preformed on the neck part comprises means for biasing the closing member to one of its positions.

6. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 5, characterized in that the biasing means comprise at least one spring. 7. Dispensing device as claimed in any of the foregoing claims, characterized by at least one pump arranged between the container and the opening, said pump having a suction side and a compression side, said dispensing device further comprising movable means connected to the pump for operating thereof, means connected to the suction side of the pump for supplying
fluid from the container and at least one discharge nozzle connected to the compression side of the pump.
8. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 7, characterized in that the part of the dispensing device preformed on the container comprises at least part of the operating means.

9. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 8, characterized in that the pump is a piston pump, the piston of the pump being connected with means for biasing it to a position of rest and the piston biasing means being attached to the container.

10. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 9, characterized in that the piston biasing means comprise at least one spring. 11. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 10, characterized in that the spring is a flexion and/or torsion spring.
12. Dispensing device, in particular as claimed in any one of claims 8 to 11, characterized in that the piston biasing means are adapted for cooperation with the operating means of the pump.
13. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 12, characterized in that the operating means are connected to the piston such as to be fixed under tension and compression.
14. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 13, characterized in that the operating means are snapped onto the piston.
15. Dispensing device as claimed in any one of the claims 7-14, characterized in that the pump has a housing to which the operating means are movably connected.
16. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 15, characterized in that the operating means comprise a trigger hingedly snapped onto the pump housing.

17. Dispensing device, in particular as claimed in any of the claims 8-13, characterized in that the pump comprises a work cylinder and a vent cylinder arranged
next thereto, and in that the operating means are arranged for displacing the pistons in these cylinders in synchronized fashion.
18. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 17, characterized in that the operating means comprise a pusher member and the or each piston is integrally formed with the pusher member.
19. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 17 or 18, characterized by means arranged in the vent cylinder for deforming the piston that is displaceable therein.
20. Dispensing device, in particular as claimed in any of the claims 8-19, characterized by blocking means cooperating with the operating means.
21. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 20, characterized in that the blocking means comprise at least one frangible tongue arranged in a path of the operating means.
22. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 21, characterized in that the or each frangible tongue is connected with the discharge nozzle.
23. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 22, characterized in that the blocking means comprise a cover closing off the discharge nozzle.
24. Dispensing device, in particular as claimed in any of the claims 8-23, characterized by a precompression system arranged between the pump and the discharge nozzle.

25. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 24, characterized in that the pump, the precompression system and part of the conduits connecting the pump to the container and/or the discharge nozzle are integrally formed.

26. Dispensing device as claimed in any of the preceding claims, characterized in that the remaining part of the dispensing device is connected by means of a snap coupling to the neck part of the container or to the part of the dispensing device preformed thereon.

27. Dispensing device as claimed in any of the claims 1-3 , characterized in that the part of the dispensing device preformed on the neck part defines a dosing chamber, and the dispensing device further comprises a feed member which is in fluid connection with the container and has at least one outlet opening, and a dosing member connected fluid-tight to the feed member and having at least one outlet opening debouching in a dosing chamber, wherein the feed member and the dosing member are rotatable relative to each other in order to determine different doses.
28. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 27, characterized in that the feed member and the dosing member each comprise a substantially cylindrical sidewall.

29. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 27 and 28, characterized in that the feed member has an axial channel recessed into its cylindrical side wall and the dosing member includes a plurality of outlet openings spaced in both peripheral and axial direction.

30. Dispensing device as claimed in any of the claims 27-29, characterized in that the dosing member is fixed in the dosing chamber and the feed member is received rotatably in the dosing chamber. 31. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 30, characterized in that the dosing member is mounted on a bottom of the dosing chamber.
32. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 31, characterized in that the dosing member is formed integrally with the bottom of the dosing chamber.

33. Dispensing device as claimed in any of the claims 27-32, characterized in that the feed member is connected to a cover at least partly closing the dosing chamber. 34. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 33, characterized in that the feed member is formed integrally with the cover.

35. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 33 or 34, characterized in that the dosing chamber has at least one outlet opening and the cover bears means for closure thereof. 36. Dispensing device as claimed in any of the claims 33-35, characterized by at least one venting aperture arranged in the cover.

38. Dispensing device as claimed in any one of the preceding claims, characterized in that the container and the part of the dispensing device preformed therewith are preformed by injection molding. 39. Dispensing device as claimed in claim 38, characterized in that the container is blow molded to an end form after the preforming.

- closing the container by connecting the remaining part of the dispensing device thereto.

45. Method as claimed in any of the claims 42- 44, characterized in that the container is preformed by means of injection molding and is blow molded into its final form prior to filling thereof.
46. Method as claimed in any of the claims 42-
45, characterized in that the container is manufactured from a resiliently deformable thermoplastic material.
47. Method as claimed in any of the claims 42-

46, characterized in that the remaining part of the dispensing device is connected by means of a snap coupling to the neck part of the container or the part of the dispensing device preformed thereon.
48. Method as claimed in any of the claims 42-
47, characterized in that the container is filled in suspended position.

49. Method as claimed in any one of the claims 42-48, characterized in that the remaining part of the dispensing device includes a pump having a displacement element that is moveable between first and second positions, the displaceable element being moved to its second position before the container is closed and being moved to its first position after the container is closed, such as to draw fluid into the pump.
